data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, the name "Nidah" refers to the holy period when a menstruating woman is considered impure and must stay away from the Masjid (mosque) and other religious gatherings. She can only resume prayers and attend religious activities once her menstrual cycle is over and she has taken a Ghusl ( ritual bath). This practice is based on Hadith and Quranic verses that emphasize the importance of cleanliness and keeping oneself pure before Allah (God).
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Nidah" holds spiritual significance as it is a reminder of the natural cycles of life and the importance of self-reflection and purification. The menstrual cycle is a reminder of the power and capacity of womanhood, and it is a time for self-care, rest, and renewal. It is also a time to remember and honor the sanctity of the body, which is a vessel for the soul and a gift from Allah.
